create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token requests may only ask for a scope that is a subset of the original authorization scope; broader scope requests are rejected.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag invalid_scope on refresh as privilege-loss or flow bug; it is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Unknown organization IDs in the urn:zitadel:iam:org:roles:id:{orgID} scope are ignored rather than causing request failure.
oidc_jwt.note: Tests expecting hard rejection for unknown org IDs will misclassify this documented ignore behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh tokens are only returned when offline_access scope was requested in the authorization code flow.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - token_endpoint / authorization code and refresh token sections
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing refresh_token as privilege reduction or token issuance bug when offline_access was not requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange defaults requested_token_type to access token when the parameter is omitted.
oidc_jwt.note: An access token response after omitting requested_token_type is by design, not evidence that the server ignored the request.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection only returns active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - introspection_endpoint
oidc_jwt.note: A non-audience client cannot use introspection as proof that a token is invalid globally.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims depending on granted scopes; missing email/profile/roles/metadata claims without corresponding scopes is by design.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat absent claims as stripping or identity confusion unless the relevant scope was granted.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims only according to granted scopes; many identity and custom claims are absent unless explicitly requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid treating missing claims as identity loss or authorization bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: A false/unauthorized introspection result from a non-audience client is expected and not evidence the token itself is invalid.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt assertions must target ZITADEL's issuing domain in aud and use a recent iat; stale or wrong-audience assertions are rejected by design.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report these rejections as unexpected proof failures; they are documented validation requirements.

oidc_jwt.description: Revocation and introspection endpoints depend on client authentication method and may reject with invalid_client when client auth is missing or malformed.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - introspection_endpoint error response; authn-methods.mdx
oidc_jwt.note: Do not confuse invalid_client with token invalidity or revocation failure.

oidc_jwt.description: In JWT IdP flow, ZITADEL does not re-authenticate the user and treats the external JWT as proof from a third-party IdP after validating signature, issuer, and expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity and claim outcomes are derived from the external JWT-backed federation flow, not from a local password or direct user login.

oidc_jwt.description: preferred_username/username is ZITADEL's login name and consists of username@primarydomain rather than the raw upstream subject value.
oidc_jwt.note: Oracle should compare against derived login-name format, not raw sent subject.

oidc_jwt.description: Using the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id} can directly redirect the user to a selected identity provider.
oidc_jwt.note: Direct IdP redirect is intended behavior and changes the observed login flow.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer assertions for service accounts/private_key_jwt require iat and it must not be older than one hour.
oidc_jwt.note: Old assertions being rejected is expected freshness enforcement, not a replay cache behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include time claims relative to the current run: use iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for a valid control token, exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} for expired-token attacks, and nbf={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for future-token attacks. Without a valid control login, a token rejection cannot be distinguished from broken client setup or bad signing.

For JWT bearer grant assertions and private_key_jwt client assertions, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}). This is exact-match audience validation, not a wildcard or pattern field. Do NOT fuzz audience-binding tests with '*' or partial URLs; use the exact issuer-domain audience for controls and a different exact audience for attacks.

For JWT bearer grant assertions and private_key_jwt client assertions, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. This is a hard freshness bound from documentation, not a defaultable hint. Use iat={{now_epoch}} for controls; assertions with iat={{now_epoch_minus_7200}} should be treated as stale-token attacks, not setup failures.

For I1 kid_injection and resign_attacker_key tests, ZITADEL identifies the signing key by the JWT header kid and validates the signature against the registered/downloaded key. A valid control assertion MUST carry the correct kid for the trusted key. Attack variants should change the signing key and/or kid, but keep all other claims valid, otherwise failures are ambiguous.

For OIDC authorization requests, nonce is REQUIRED for implicit flow and strongly recommended for code flow to bind the client session to the ID token and mitigate replay. For I2/OIDC replay-related tests, the fuzzer MUST send a nonce on start_oidc_auth and verify the returned id_token corresponds to that request context; omitting nonce can create false positives about replay acceptance.

For OIDC flow-coherence tests, state MUST be sent on start_oidc_auth and tracked through the callback. The docs mark state as CSRF mitigation and the authorize response returns the unmodified state. Tests like state_swap or code_injection are only meaningful if each browser session uses a distinct state and the fuzzer verifies the returned state matches the initiating session.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, code_challenge_method supports only the exact value S256. There is no documented alternative mode or disable sentinel. A valid PKCE control request MUST use code_challenge_method=S256 on authorize and the matching code_verifier on token exchange; otherwise token failures are setup errors, not security findings.

For redirect_uri_mismatch and general code-flow controls, redirect_uri must match exactly between the authorization request and token request, and must exactly match a preregistered redirect URI. This is exact string matching only; wildcards are not documented. Do NOT attempt multi-URI tests with pattern values. Use distinct exact redirect URIs per scenario.

For token exchange audience-binding tests, audience on /oauth/v2/token token-exchange requests MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. Therefore, a valid control must first obtain subject/actor tokens whose audiences already cover the requested audience. If not, rejection is by design and must not be reported as a vulnerability.

For token exchange type tests, supported token-type combinations are constrained by ZITADEL's matrix: refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token, actor_token, or requested_token_type; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; JWT as subject_token is only allowed in combination with actor_token; user_id subject_token is only allowed with actor_token. The fuzzer MUST respect this matrix or treat rejections as expected setup failures.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on refresh or token exchange, requested scope cannot exceed prior authorization. Refresh-token scope must be a subset of the original scope, and token-exchange invalid_scope errors are expected when requested scope exceeds what the resource owner granted. A valid escalation test must compare exchanged-token claims against the original granted scope, not merely request broader scope and treat rejection as a bug.

For introspection-based verification, active=true is only returned when the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. Therefore, introspect_token MUST authenticate as a client that is in the token's audience. Otherwise active=false or 401 invalid_client is expected and must not be interpreted as token invalidity or freshness failure.

For revocation tests, /oauth/v2/introspect is the documented way to distinguish revoked from merely expired tokens because local JWT validation cannot detect revocation. A correct I2 revocation sequence should revoke the token, then introspect it with an authorized audience client and expect active=false. Do not rely only on JWT signature/exp checks after revoke.

For OIDC RP validation tests involving external IdPs or JWT IdP-style upstream assertions, ZITADEL documentation explicitly states it verifies signature, issuer, and expiration of the consumed JWT. Therefore, I1 trust-anchor-substitution, resign_attacker_key, and issuer-substitution tests must vary exactly one of these inputs at a time while keeping the others valid; otherwise failures are not attributable to the intended invariant.

For JWT IdP browser-proxy flows, the upstream JWT must be delivered in an HTTP header and the proxy must forward all original query parameters intact to ZITADEL's receiving endpoint. Any test that drops or rewrites query parameters breaks OIDC flow state and causes by-design failures unrelated to proof validation or session binding.

Reserved scope values such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:roles:id:{orgID}, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud are exact literal scope strings with embedded identifiers, not wildcard-capable matchers. For multi-identity or multi-org tests, the fuzzer MUST generate exact scope strings per scenario; using '*' or partial scope prefixes will not broaden matching and will instead request a different literal scope.

When using the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname}, ZITADEL enforces organization membership and may fail the login if the organization does not exist or the user is not a member. For I4 principal-binding tests across multiple identities, omit these org-restricting scopes unless the test specifically targets org membership, otherwise cross-user differences may be caused by scope-enforced org filtering rather than identity mapping.

When using the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:roles:id:{orgID}, unknown organization IDs are ignored. Therefore, I5 tests that expect denial from an unknown org-role limiter will produce false positives if they assume unknown IDs are rejecting. The oracle must treat omission/ignore behavior as by design and verify returned role claims rather than expecting an error.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include a valid control token alongside attack variants. Use a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, aud including the ZITADEL issuing domain, and matching iss/sub from the service account or application key. Without a control, token endpoint failure cannot be distinguished from broken client setup or bad client identity.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} per docs examples). Do NOT use the token endpoint URL as aud unless separately documented; tests for issuer/trust-anchor substitution must keep aud pointed at the ZITADEL issuer domain or failures may be caused by audience mismatch instead of the intended invariant.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT iat claim MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. This is a hard freshness requirement from the docs. Use iat={{now_epoch}} for controls and future/expired variants relative to that; otherwise ZITADEL may reject the assertion before evaluating the attack condition under test.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header MUST contain kid set to the downloaded keyId. Omitting or altering kid can cause key lookup failure, which would confound I1 signature-validation tests such as resign_attacker_key or kid_injection.

For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests against login_with_jwt, keep iss and sub equal to the documented key owner identity from the downloaded key material (service account userId for JWT bearer grant; clientId for private_key_jwt auth) and keep aud valid. Otherwise rejection may be due to subject/client mismatch rather than proof validation.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of a bug. A valid negative test must compare an in-subset audience control against an out-of-subset attack.

For token_exchange, requested_token_type defaults to access token when omitted. Do NOT interpret an access_token response after omitting requested_token_type as the server ignoring the parameter; omission is documented default behavior.
For token_exchange, resource is currently not supported. Do NOT use resource-based attack variants or treat rejection/ignoring of resource as a security finding.

Token exchange token-type support is restricted by documented matrix: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; user_id is allowed only with actor_token. Tests MUST stay within supported combinations for controls, otherwise failures are by design.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, refresh_token is only returned when offline_access scope was requested, and refresh-token grant scopes must be a subset of the original scope. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token without offline_access as a bug, and use original-scope subset controls when testing scope narrowing or expansion.

For OIDC authorization-code flow coherence tests, redirect_uri must match exactly between authorize and token requests and must exactly match a preregistered redirect URI. Any mismatch rejection is by design and should not be reported as an I3 inconsistency.
For OIDC authorization requests, openid scope is mandatory. Any request missing openid may fail with invalid_scope by design; do not use missing-openid requests as controls for unrelated invariants.
For OIDC implicit-flow tests, nonce MUST be provided. Missing nonce in implicit flow is invalid by design and cannot be used to infer replay or signature-validation behavior.

For OIDC RP validation tests, nonce should always be sent even in authorization-code controls because ZITADEL documents it as recommended to bind the client session to the ID token and mitigate replay. A valid I2 nonce test must compare matching-nonce control versus mismatched or missing-nonce attack under otherwise identical conditions.

For JWT IdP browser-mediated login flows, the upstream proxy/WAF MUST forward all original query parameters intact when redirecting/proxying to /idps/jwt. Dropping state, nonce, or other OIDC parameters breaks flow state and can create false I3 failures unrelated to JWT validation.
For JWT IdP, the external JWT MUST be delivered in the configured HTTP header, never as a URL parameter. Tests that place the JWT in query parameters are invalid setup and any rejection is by design.

For JWT IdP I1 tests, ZITADEL documents three validation checks on the external JWT: signature must validate using the Keys Endpoint, iss must match configured issuer, and the JWT must not be expired. Controls and attacks must isolate one of these checks at a time; otherwise failures are ambiguous.

For JWT IdP trust-anchor rotation tests, the trusted verification material comes from the configured Keys Endpoint and may be cached by clients, but ZITADEL docs only state that keys can rotate without prior notice and kid is set properly. Do not assume stale-key acceptance is a vulnerability unless the old key remains accepted after explicit trust rotation and any relevant cache has been refreshed or expired.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false or limited introspection result from a non-audience client is by design; audience-mismatch controls are required before claiming I5 audience bypass.

For introspect_token and token endpoint client authentication, ZITADEL supports client_secret_basic and private_key_jwt. If using client_secret_basic, client_id and client_secret in the Basic header must be form-url-encoded before base64 encoding. Incorrect encoding causes invalid_client and is not a security finding.

For I2 replay_same_token against login_with_jwt, JWT bearer replay protection via jti tracking is not documented. Treat repeated acceptance of the same JWT bearer assertion as inconclusive unless the specific context is documented to require one-time use; otherwise this is likely stateless JWT behavior rather than a vulnerability.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT bearer grants, ZITADEL requires iat and enforces that it MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. A login failure with an old assertion may be caused by iat-age enforcement rather than exp/nbf logic. Keep control assertions within the last hour when isolating exp or nbf behavior.

For I1 issuer/audience validation of JWT bearer grants, the assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (for example https://{domain}). If aud does not include the issuer domain, token exchange/login failures are expected and do not demonstrate a security check bypass.

For I1 key-selection tests on JWT bearer grants, the JWT header kid MUST identify the uploaded/downloaded keyId. ZITADEL documentation states the kid header is necessary to identify the key. Missing or wrong kid can cause expected rejection unrelated to the invariant under test.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience exceeds that subset, rejection is by design and must not be treated as a vulnerability.

For token_exchange tests, requested_token_type defaults to access token when omitted. If the fuzzer is testing wrong-token-type acceptance, it MUST set requested_token_type explicitly; otherwise success may simply reflect the documented default.

For token_exchange token-type tests, ZITADEL supports only the documented matrix: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; user_id is allowed only with actor_token. Rejections outside this matrix are by design.

For I5 scope-escalation tests using refresh_token or token_exchange, ZITADEL documents that requested scope on refresh_token MUST be a subset of the originally requested scope, and token endpoint may reject invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds the granted scope. Treat such rejection as expected enforcement, not a bug.

For verify_granted_identity, claims returned by /oidc/v1/userinfo depend on granted scopes. Missing email/profile/roles/metadata claims are expected unless the corresponding scopes were requested. I4/I5 comparisons MUST request the needed scopes first.

For I5 role/metadata claim tests, ZITADEL-specific claims are scope-gated: urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:roles requires corresponding role scopes or project configuration; urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata requires scope urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata and values are base64 encoded. Do not treat absent claims without scopes as authorization failures.

For I4 identity verification, /userinfo returns sub as the stable subject identifier and preferred_username as ZITADEL login name in the form username@primarydomain when that scope/claim is available. Do not assume display_name equals the JWT bearer assertion sub for machine/service-account flows.

For OIDC authorization-flow tests, redirect_uri matching is exact at both authorize and token exchange. A mismatch is documented to produce invalid_grant/authorization failure and is expected behavior, not an I3 flaw.

For OIDC implicit-flow tests, nonce MUST be provided. ZITADEL documents nonce as MUST for implicit flow. Missing nonce causing failure is expected and should not be interpreted as stronger replay protection bypass or identity confusion.

For OIDC authorization requests, state is only recommended, not required. Tests for state-swap or CSRF defenses MUST include a control request with state set; omitting state and observing no state validation is not evidence of a vulnerability because the parameter is optional by design.

For OIDC RP-style tests involving external IdPs or JWT IdP preselection, ZITADEL may redirect directly to an IdP when the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id} is present. This changes the login path by design; the fuzzer must account for direct-redirect behavior when modeling multi-step flow coherence.

For JWT IdP browser-proxy integrations, the upstream JWT MUST be delivered in an HTTP header, never as a URL parameter, and all original query parameters must be forwarded intact to /idps/jwt. If query parameters are dropped, OIDC state can break and produce false I3 failures unrelated to JWT validation.

For JWT IdP tests, the JWT endpoint should be on the same domain as the existing app/WAF so browser cookies are sent automatically. Missing cookies can prevent JWT issuance and cause login failure unrelated to ZITADEL's JWT validation logic.

For JWT IdP validation tests, documented checks are signature validation using the configured keys endpoint, issuer equality against configured issuer, and expiration enforcement. The fuzzer MUST ensure the keys endpoint, issuer, and header name are configured correctly before attributing acceptance/rejection to a security invariant.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is authorized and part of the token audience. A false/unauthorized introspection result can be caused by client-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity. Use a client in the token audience for control introspection.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
